topics.label: Introduction to the complement lecture
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the opening framing, administrative context, and preliminary overview of the lecture on complement.

topics.label: Fundamentals and core principles of the complement system
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the foundational concepts, naming conventions, and central role of C3 activation governing the complement cascade.

topics.label: Pathways of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the upstream recognition pathways and mechanisms that drive complement activation to reach a critical threshold on target surfaces.

topics.label: Effector mechanisms of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the downstream effector processes through which activated complement neutralizes pathogens and drives inflammation.

topics.label: Host regulation of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the regulatory proteins and inhibitory mechanisms that protect host cells from inadvertent complement attack.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic analyzes how deficiencies in individual complement components and regulators lead to distinct clinical presentations.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines the molecular strategies that pathogens, such as Staphylococcus aureus, use to evade complement-mediated destruction.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the concluding closing remarks and previews the next lecture on the adaptive immune system.
